key_insight: DiffVortex compresses the Biot–Savart kernel rather than the flow state, combining tensor-network acceleration with flexible Lagrangian vortex simulation.
engineering_relevance: Its differentiable GPU implementation supports flow simulation around moving and deforming bodies, with gradients through time integration for potential design optimization.
method: Evolve vorticity as Lagrangian particles and represent immersed bodies with bound vortex sheets.
Use quantics tensor cross interpolation to precompute tensor-network contractions for fast multipole moment-to-local translation.
Prove that kernel QTT rank r yields convolution MPO rank at most 2^d r, independent of grid resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on an impulsively started cylinder and inviscid elliptical vortices, demonstrations with moving and deforming bodies, and capacity for 6.7×10^7 particles on one GPU.
watch_item: Practical speed and memory gains depend on keeping tensor ranks manageable; the rank bound alone does not establish resolution-independent total simulation cost.
paper_title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
